question:
Figure 1 is the golden sample and figure 2 is the part under test. The two frames are pixel-aligned, but figure 2 was shot under noticeably different lighting, so large areas of the two images differ in brightness without anything being wrong with the part. Ignoring the lighting difference, at most one of the candidate regions below contains a real manufacturing defect. Regions are normalized [x1, y1, x2, y2] in [0, 1] (origin top-left). Which region contains a real defect?
(A) [0.0025, 0.3282, 0.2025, 0.5282]
(B) [0.3282, 0.2011, 0.5282, 0.4011]
(C) [0.3316, 0.4271, 0.5316, 0.6271]
(D) No real defect — the two frames differ only in lighting.

Answer with only the correct option letter.
